keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 5,087 km2 disc (centroid 73.31E 33.46N) lies on the Rawalpindi plateau beside Taxila, about 90 km west of Rajouri, where Cliopatria puts its Gandhara disc (74.37E 33.39N): the two rows look swapped (the Gandhara dossier of sa-01 says the same). The pages place the Kambojas 'in the Kabul Valley' (Liebich) or 'from Kafiristan to the southwestern part of Kashmir' (Lamotte) (Kambojas page) and 'from Nurestan up to Rajauri' (Mahajanapadas page). Neither page has an infobox area. The correction takes the three places the pages name, Nuristan, Kapisa (Begram) and a 50 km circle at Rajouri (the radius is my reading), and cuts out the Gandhara dossier's land. The first version overlapped it: the Rajouri circle took 6 cells of the Kashmir Valley (Gandhara's 'valley of Kasmira', -600..-519) and Nuristan 2 cells of the Gandhara region (the Peshawar valley, Gandhara to -536, Achaemenid Gandara from -535). Corrected after the adversarial review of 2026-10-18: the union minus the Kashmir Valley and Gandhara regions, 58 cells, about 16,600 km2 (3.3 times the disc), in three pieces (Nuristan 30 cells, Rajouri 22, Kapisa 6), with 0 cells shared with the Gandhara dossier's -600 keyframe (249 cells) or the old Cliopatria disc. The Kambojas page does not name the Kashmir valley as Kamboja's (only Lamotte's 'the southwestern part of Kashmir'), so the line between Rajouri and the Valley is my reading and the Gandhara owner (sa-01-a) may move it.

notes: Both Cliopatria Kamboja shapes are the same 5,087 km2 disc on the Rawalpindi plateau; the Mahajanapadas page puts the capital at Rajori (Rajouri), where Cliopatria's Gandhara discs sit, and the Gandhara dossier flags the swap too. Both shapes are marked adjust: Nuristan, Kapisa and a 50 km circle at Rajouri to -531, then without Kapisa to -501. The Kambojas page is thin on place and date (no infobox, no area, no founding; 'Kabul Valley' per Liebich, 'Kafiristan to the southwestern part of Kashmir' per Lamotte, capital 'site remains unknown'). The Achaemenid conquest page does not name the Kambojas as a satrapy (its lists give Gandara, Sattagydia, Hindush; Herodotus's twentieth province is 'the Indians') against the Mahajanapadas page's 'twentieth and richest satrapy' of Kamboja and Gandhara: the end at -501 is Cliopatria's year and rests on that undated sentence, confidence 1. Unsettled: whether Rajouri was ever Persian; the relation of Kamboja to Gandhara. The Kambojas page also places them in Ashoka's time beside Greeks and Gandharans (outside this window). Pages: Kambojas, Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley and the shared Mahajanapadas page (budget 1-2 plus the shared page). Gazetteer lacks: Rajouri (place, 33.38N 74.31E, also Rajauri/Rajori, Rajapura); Kafiristan (alias of Nuristan) and the Hindu Kush. Repair of 2026-10-18 (after the adversarial review): the first corrected land overlapped the Gandhara dossier (Rajouri 50 km took 6 cells of its Kashmir Valley, Nuristan 2 cells of its Gandhara region); both keyframes, the found and dissolve events and the Achaemenid successor land now subtract {Kashmir Valley, Gandhara}, leaving 58 cells (-600..-531, about 16,600 km2) and 52 cells (-530..-501, about 14,900 km2) and no cell shared with the Gandhara dossier. The Mahajanapadas and Kambojas pages were reopened: neither places the Kashmir valley in Kamboja, so the Pir Panjal line is my reading and open to agreement with the Gandhara owner (sa-01-a). The land is still three separate pieces (Nuristan, Kapisa, Rajouri), because the pages name only those places. The Gandhara dossier also leaves the Kashmir Valley to nobody after -518, which this dossier does not contradict.
